source.title: Illustrative scenario 01: a fingertip measure
source.annotation: An explicitly invented scenario for testing how a source connects to a specific passage. No interview was conducted. This is not a bibliographic reference or evidence of a cultural practice.

content.title: measuring with a fingertip
content.summary: A familiar hand becomes a measure. A small adjustment, each time the pot changes.
content.context: In this fictional example, a cook learns by watching a relative rather than reading a recipe. The account describes one household routine, not a rule for any community.
content.account: Level the rice in the pot. Rest a fingertip on the surface, then add water to a familiar point on the finger. Adjust for the pot and the rice.
content.judgement: The useful measure comes from trying, tasting, and remembering. A different pot or grain can change what works.

interpretation.author: Source Culture demo editor (fictional)
interpretation.text: One possible reading is measurement through a bodily reference, followed by adjustment from experience. This describes one aspect of the scenario; it does not explain the whole practice.

content.title: one row, then another
content.summary: Keeping a small repeating pattern in your hands, without keeping count of everything.
content.context: This fictional contributor practises a small knitting repeat, using the feel of the last stitch as a reminder of the next.
content.account: Work a short sequence of knit and purl stitches. Look at the row below before starting the next repeat. Pause when the surface stops matching the expected pattern.
content.judgement: The texture acts as a check. A misplaced stitch can be found by looking back, rather than counting every stitch.
content.reuse: illustrative development content; no collection-wide reuse licence

content.title: a rhythm learned by watching
content.summary: Listen, copy, miss a beat, try again. A sequence remembered together.
content.context: An invented scenario of two friends learning a clapping game by copying each other. No particular traditional game is being documented.
content.account: Start with a clap. Tap hands with a partner. Clap twice, pause, and repeat. Slow down together when the sequence slips.
content.judgement: Success is a shared rhythm, rather than a fixed speed. A pause gives both players a way back into the sequence.
content.reuse: illustrative development content; no collection-wide reuse licence

content.title: turn where the road gets quiet
content.summary: Remembering a route through landmarks, sounds, and the shape of a corner.
content.context: This fictional walk is remembered through a sequence of noticeable changes. It is not an account of a real neighbourhood.
content.account: Walk to the large tree, turn at the narrow passage, and listen for the quieter street. Describe the route again after walking it.
content.judgement: A landmark can change. Remembering several cues gives another way to recognise the same turn.
content.reuse: illustrative development content; no collection-wide reuse licence

content.title: a place in the circle
content.summary: An object moves from hand to hand, carrying the next turn with it.
content.context: An illustrative group uses a small object to make the order of turns visible. This is a fictional example, not a claim of origin.
content.account: Choose an order together. Give the object to the first person. Pass it along after each turn. Agree what happens when someone skips.
content.judgement: The object makes the current turn visible; the group still negotiates pauses and exceptions.
content.reuse: illustrative development content; no collection-wide reuse licence

content.title: the recipe that isn’t written down
content.summary: Remembering the order by the way ingredients feel, sound, and change.
content.context: A fictional account of learning a simple dish through repeated practice. The description is intentionally incomplete as a cooking recipe.
content.account: Notice each change as the ingredients cook. Use those changes to remember when to take the next action.
content.judgement: Smell, texture, and sound can be useful cues. This imagined account cannot stand in for the judgement of an experienced cook.
content.reuse: illustrative development content; no collection-wide reuse licence

content.title: the same cup, every time
content.summary: Another way to find the balance: a familiar cup and a remembered proportion.
content.context: A fictional variation on the fingertip example. Here, the contributor keeps the container constant instead of using a hand as a reference.
content.account: Use one familiar cup for the rice and the water. Begin with the proportion that worked last time. Make a note when the grain or pot changes.
content.judgement: The consistency comes partly from returning to the same cup. The result still needs to be checked.
